title: The Electric Fleet Size and Mix Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows and Recharging Stations
core_evidence: ALNS with Resize and RelocateAndResize; insertion can change vehicle type; fixed-order labeling repositions charging stations
complexity_evidence: Same-type bounded-sequence moves can be evaluated in O(1); changing vehicle type requires linear recomputation of affected sequence
portability_evidence: Method can be reimplemented from the paper but no author code repository was found in either research cycle
notes: The paper assumes full linear recharge and at most one charging station between adjacent non-CS nodes; it is not sufficient for ReSETP nonlinear partial charging by itself.

title: Improved formulations and algorithmic components for the electric vehicle routing problem with nonlinear charging functions
core_evidence: Exact label-setting algorithm solves fixed-route charging with piecewise-linear concave charging functions; allows multiple charging-station visits between non-CS nodes
complexity_evidence: FRVCP is NP-hard and label count is exponential in the worst case; dominance and preprocessing gave about 1 ms average on 29443 literature routes
portability_evidence: Strong algorithmic fit as an affected-route oracle; model and objective adapters are required
notes: The article reports that revising charging decisions alone improved 23 of 120 prior best-known E-VRP-NL solutions.

title: frvcpy: An Open-Source Solver for the Fixed Route Vehicle Charging Problem
core_evidence: Open Python implementation of the Froger label-setting algorithm; supports nonlinear piecewise-linear charging functions, heterogeneous charging technologies and multiple CS visits
complexity_evidence: Paper reports 5.6 ms average in its software test; exact method retains exponential worst-case behavior
portability_evidence: Python API is directly probeable; ReSETP units, time windows, costs, station capacity and nonlinear curve contract require an explicit adapter
notes: Software functionality was independently reproduced in Python 3.13; no ReSETP solver file was imported or changed.

title: e-VRO/frvcpy release repository
core_evidence: Version 0.1.1 source contains label and SOC-function implementation and depends only on xmltodict
complexity_evidence: Repository does not state a polynomial bound; implementation follows the exact label-setting method
portability_evidence: Installs and runs on the project's Python 3.13 host inside an isolated temporary virtual environment
notes: Repository last visible commit is 2021-06-01; maintenance staleness is a migration risk.

title: INFORMS Journal on Computing software snapshot 2020.1035
core_evidence: Publication snapshot contains paper-linked source, instances, scripts and results
complexity_evidence: Used to verify the software-paper lineage rather than performance
portability_evidence: Useful as immutable reference snapshot; current package repository is FC-S04
notes: The snapshot and e-VRO release agree on Apache-2.0 licensing.

title: PyVRP
core_evidence: Supports heterogeneous vehicle types with capacities, fixed and variable costs, time limits, profiles and multi-depot routing; local search includes exchange, relocate and tail-swap families
complexity_evidence: Granular local search evaluates bounded sequence changes using cached route segments; whole search remains heuristic
portability_evidence: C++ core with Python API; high engineering quality, but SOC and charging are not native and direct code embedding would create a large integration surface
notes: Version 0.13.4 was probed in an isolated Python 3.13 environment; candidate is an engineering reference or external baseline, not a drop-in charging solver.

title: PyVRP: a high-performance VRP solver package
core_evidence: Documents the solver architecture and high-performance local-search components
complexity_evidence: Performance evidence is for supported VRP variants, not for SOC-constrained EV routing
portability_evidence: Supports using PyVRP as a source for tested route-neighborhood and cache design
notes: No claim is made that PyVRP already solves ReSETP.

title: The Heterogeneous-Fleet Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with Nonlinear Charging Functions
core_evidence: Evaluates each customer route under every EV type; uses nonlinear route evaluation, ReplacePath charging-path neighborhood, bounded route pool and set-partitioning assembly
complexity_evidence: FRVCP is identified as NP-hard; the paper's heuristic route evaluator avoids exact FRVCP at every move, while set partitioning grows exponentially with pool size
portability_evidence: Highest conceptual match, but no official source repository was found; reimplementation and independent verification would be required
notes: The paper reports 32 new BKS on E-VRP-NL and 33 on E-FSMFTW-PR; those are literature results, not reproduced ReSETP results.

title: The heterogeneous-fleet electric vehicle routing problem with nonlinear charging functions
core_evidence: Public working paper exposes route-evaluation algorithms, six VND neighborhoods, ReplacePath and route-pool filtering details
complexity_evidence: States exponential FRVCP and SP growth; gives explicit route-pool cap and heuristic-evaluation rationale
portability_evidence: Sufficient to design a clean-room method probe, not to copy source code
notes: GERAD permits private research download but not redistribution of the PDF; only URL and findings are recorded here.

title: The Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with Nonlinear Charging Functions
core_evidence: Set-partitioning branch-price-and-cut and tabu-search heuristic simultaneously evaluate routing and piecewise-linear nonlinear charging
complexity_evidence: Exact method solves reported instances up to 40 customers; tabu search improved larger benchmark results
portability_evidence: Useful as an independent validation source for nonlinear resource recursions; no official implementation was identified
notes: Only the 2021 arXiv preprint metadata was verified; no journal publication is claimed.

title: Current ReSETP fleet and charging mechanisms
core_evidence: Existing protected kernel registers vehicle_type_swap, charging_station_reset_destroy, low_carbon_charging_repair and a diagnostic fleet_charge_corepair
complexity_evidence: G0 audit has not closed all complete-solution score sites; performance comparison is not authorized
portability_evidence: Any future candidate must be isolated until E7 ends and G0 passes
notes: Read-only audit only; protected files were not modified.
